checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can blocks with zero blob KZG commitments be incorrectly rejected?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths that validate blob KZG commitments in block processing. 2. Create a test block with zero blob KZG commitments and verify it is accepted as valid. 3. Verify there is no explicit lower bound check (e.g., len(commitments) >= 1) that would incorrectly reject empty commitment lists. 4. Check block validation functions for any conditional logic that might inadvertently require at least one commitment. 5. Test edge cases: empty commitment list, null commitment field, and missing commitment field to ensure consistent valid handling. 6. Review error handling to confirm no false rejection occurs for zero commitments.
checklist.invariant_statement: Blocks with zero blob KZG commitments MUST be considered valid. There is no lower bound check on the number of commitments.
checklist.falsification_goal: Attempt to find code paths where a block with zero KZG commitments is incorrectly rejected, violating the invariant that empty commitment lists are valid.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0027. This invariant ensures that blocks without blob transactions (and thus zero KZG commitments) remain valid per the EIP-4844 specification. A violation could cause consensus failures if nodes incorrectly reject valid blocks.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange enforce response size limits (count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS and MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the DataColumnSidecarsByRange request handler in the P2P layer. 2. Identify where the response is constructed and sidecars are added. 3. Verify that the handler enforces the limit: response.sidecars.len() <= count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS. 4. Verify that the handler enforces the absolute limit: response.sidecars.len() <= MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. 5. Test with boundary values: request count=0, count=1, count=MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB. 6. Test with adversarial requests: verify that even if more sidecars are available, only the allowed maximum is returned. 7. Check for integer overflow in count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS calculation. 8. Verify that malicious peers cannot cause the node to send oversized responses that would get it penalized.
checklist.invariant_statement: DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses MUST contain no more than count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars AND no more than MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS sidecars total.
checklist.falsification_goal: Attempt to trigger a DataColumnSidecarsByRange response that exceeds either the count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS limit or the MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS absolute limit, violating the response size invariant.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0028. This invariant guards the P2P trust boundary by limiting response sizes. Violation could lead to: (1) bandwidth exhaustion attacks, (2) peer penalization if oversized responses are sent, (3) protocol non-compliance. The dual constraint (count-based and absolute max) must both be enforced.

checklist.title: Verify DataColumnSidecarsByRange Response Ordering: Are sidecars returned in deterministic (slot, column_index) order?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the DataColumnSidecarsByRange request handler in the P2P layer. 2. Review the code that constructs responses to verify ordering logic. 3. Craft multiple requests spanning different slot ranges and column indices. 4. Verify responses are always ordered by (slot, column_index) tuple - first by ascending slot, then by ascending column_index within each slot. 5. Test edge cases: empty ranges, single sidecar responses, maximum range requests. 6. Verify ordering is deterministic across repeated identical requests. 7. Check for any code paths that could return out-of-order results (e.g., concurrent collection modifications, unstable sorts). 8. Attempt to trigger race conditions that might affect ordering consistency.
checklist.invariant_statement: For all DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses R, for all indices i < j in R: (R[i].slot < R[j].slot) OR (R[i].slot == R[j].slot AND R[i].column_index < R[j].column_index)
checklist.falsification_goal: Attempt to trigger non-deterministic ordering by: (a) requesting large ranges that stress sorting/collection logic, (b) making concurrent requests to expose race conditions in response construction, (c) testing boundary conditions where slot/column_index values are at extremes (0, max values), (d) examining if any caching or parallel processing could return results out of order.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0029. This ordering guarantee is critical for protocol correctness - clients may rely on deterministic ordering for efficient processing, caching, or verification. Violations could lead to consensus issues or enable DoS vectors if clients cannot properly handle out-of-order responses.

checklist.title: Verify DataColumnSidecarsByRange Response Atomicity: Are ALL sidecars from a block included when ANY sidecar from that block is returned?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the DataColumnSidecarsByRange handler implementation in the P2P layer. 2. Review the response construction logic - identify where sidecars are collected for inclusion. 3. Verify there is no early termination or filtering that could return partial sidecars (e.g., rate limiting, size limits, timeout). 4. Check for error paths that could return partial data (e.g., database read failures mid-block). 5. Test edge cases: request spanning multiple blocks where the last block has incomplete data. 6. Verify that if ANY sidecar from block B is included, ALL sidecars from block B are included - count(included_sidecars[block]) == count(available_sidecars[block]) OR count(included_sidecars[block]) == 0. 7. Fuzz the handler with range requests that hit size/count limits to verify block-level atomicity is preserved. 8. Check for race conditions where sidecars are being written while a range request is being served.
checklist.invariant_statement: For DataColumnSidecarsByRange, if any sidecar from a block is included in the response, ALL sidecars from that block MUST be included.
checklist.falsification_goal: Attempt to trigger a DataColumnSidecarsByRange response that contains partial sidecars for a block by: (a) hitting response size limits mid-block, (b) causing storage I/O failures during response construction, (c) exploiting race conditions during concurrent sidecar writes and reads.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030. This atomicity invariant ensures data availability sampling works correctly in PeerDAS/Fusaka. If partial sidecars are returned, a node might incorrectly conclude data is unavailable (false negative) or make incorrect DA sampling decisions. This could cause a node to reject valid blocks or accept invalid ones, leading to consensus forks.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can DataColumnSidecarsByRange be made to return partial block sidecars through resource exhaustion?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify any response size limits (MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE) or item count limits (MAX_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_PER_BLOCK). 2. Craft a request where including all sidecars from a block would exceed the limit. 3. Verify the handler either: (a) excludes the entire block, or (b) returns an error, but NEVER returns partial sidecars. 4. Test with concurrent requests to induce race conditions. 5. Test with storage I/O errors mid-read to verify partial reads do not leak into responses. 6. Monitor logs/metrics for any 'partial sidecar' warnings that might indicate violated invariants.
checklist.invariant_statement: For DataColumnSidecarsByRange, if any sidecar from a block is included in the response, ALL sidecars from that block MUST be included.
checklist.falsification_goal: Specifically target the atomicity invariant through resource boundary conditions: craft requests that would cause the response to hit size/count limits exactly mid-block, forcing a decision between (a) including partial sidecars (violation), (b) excluding the entire block (correct), or (c) returning error (acceptable).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030. This is a focused falsification test specifically targeting the atomicity invariant through resource boundary conditions. The interaction between PROP-0028 (size limits) and PROP-0030 (atomicity) must be tested together to ensure limits are enforced at block boundaries, not sidecar boundaries.

checklist.title: Verify Fork Choice Consistency: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange terminate the stream when fork choice changes?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the DataColumnSidecarsByRange RPC handler implementation and locate where sidecars are retrieved for streaming. 2. Trace how the handler determines which sidecars are from the 'current fork choice chain' - identify the fork choice head reference. 3. Identify the fork choice change detection mechanism: is there a listener, callback, or polling mechanism? 4. Simulate a fork choice update (reorg) during an active sidecar stream by: (a) starting a range request, (b) triggering a fork choice change mid-stream via late block arrival or reorg, (c) observing stream behavior. 5. Verify the stream terminates gracefully upon fork choice change rather than: (a) returning stale sidecars from the old canonical chain, (b) continuing to stream as if nothing changed, (c) returning a mix of old and new chain sidecars. 6. Check for race conditions between fork choice updates and sidecar retrieval - verify proper locking/synchronization. 7. Test edge cases: fork choice change at stream start, at stream end, and mid-stream. 8. Verify no sidecars from orphaned/non-canonical blocks are returned after fork choice change. 9. Check that the termination is clean (no partial data, proper error signaling to peer).
checklist.invariant_statement: DataColumnSidecarsByRange sidecars MUST be from the current fork choice chain. If fork choice changes during response, the stream MUST terminate.
checklist.falsification_goal: Attempt to trigger inconsistent sidecar delivery by: (a) causing a reorg during an active DataColumnSidecarsByRange stream, (b) verifying whether stale sidecars from the old chain are returned, (c) checking if the stream continues despite fork choice change, (d) observing if mixed sidecars from old and new chains are returned. Any of these outcomes would falsify the invariant.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0031. This invariant ensures data availability sampling (DAS) consistency in PeerDAS. Violation could cause peers to receive sidecars that are no longer canonical, potentially leading to: (1) consensus divergence if nodes make DA decisions based on stale data, (2) wasted bandwidth transferring non-canonical data, (3) confusion in sync protocols expecting canonical chain data. The fork choice change detection mechanism is critical - verify it uses proper locking/synchronization to prevent TOCTOU race conditions.
